items.description: Tool search MCP profile: the default tools plus getToolSearchPage, which finds the tools for an action instead of reading the catalogue. Needs Elasticsearch or OpenSearch.
items.instructions: These tools reach every operation Liferay exposes, through a catalogue far too large to read. Start with getToolSearchPage: pass what the user wants to do as "search" and it returns the most relevant tools, ranked. Set includeRequiredInputSchema and the top result carries the arguments it cannot run without, so postToolSetToolSetNameToolInvoke can follow immediately; call getToolSetToolSetNameTool first only when optional arguments are needed too. A search result names an operation reachable through this server, not a tool you can call: run it with postToolSetToolSetNameToolInvoke, passing the result's toolSetName and name. The tools listed here are the only ones that exist, so calling a name from a result as though it were one of them fails. Search covers one action, so a request spanning several steps needs one search per step. Count the repetitions before you search: when the same operation would run ten or more times, say so in the search, as in "add twenty books at once", and prefer the batch operation that comes back. It answers 202 with an import task rather than a result, so confirm it by invoking getImportTask in headless-batch-engine-v1.0 with the id it returned, rather than searching for a way to check. An operation can also be turned off on the instance it is reached through, and nothing in a search result says so. Two answers mean exactly that and are final: one naming a disabled feature flag, as in "Feature flag LPD-35443 is disabled for company 38371352027067", and one reporting an UnsupportedOperationException. Treat either as a wall. Stop that step immediately. Do not invoke the same tool again, do not invoke an operation in another tool set whose name resembles it, do not invoke its batch form, and do not search for a way around it: they all reach the same switch, and every attempt costs a round trip and ends the same way. Tell the user which feature is off, name the flag if the answer named one, say which step could not be done, and carry on with the steps that do not depend on it. A result may list prerequisites, naming what its path needs identified before it can be invoked and, where the parameter accepts something you already hold, saying so. Read them rather than searching for the same thing again.Search in the words a user would use, not Liferay's: a published object definition exposes its entries under the object's own name, so "create a pet store" finds them and "create an object entry" does not. The reverse holds for a kind of thing Liferay does not model at all: nothing creates a ticket or a webinar, so when creating one finds nothing plausible, define an object definition for it and use the tool set that publishing it registers. Do not open the catalogue to begin with. getToolSetsPage and getToolSetToolSetNameToolSummariesPage list every tool-set and every operation within one, costing many times the context of a search; use them only after a search has returned nothing relevant.
items.name: tool-search
